newsitem.title: UK: London gold easier, seen testing support.
newsitem.headline: London gold easier, seen testing support.

text.p: Gold prices edged lower on Friday, cautiously testing the strength of the nearby support level after climbing higher earlier in the week.
"Gold has a support line at $382-$382.50 and if it breaks that it will target below $380," a dealer said. "But giving it the benefit of the doubt, it will hold here and move higher."
Bullion fixed at $382.20 an ounce, compared with $383.00 on Thursday afternoon and a London close of $382.80/$383.30.

Trading was quiet in early Europe, with the New York opening awaited for a clue to the market's next move, dealers said. Gold, with the rest of the precious metals in tow, had notched up about $4.00 at the start of the week in an apparent recovery from a downtrend since early September.
But a tumble in silver prices on Thursday afternoon dragged gold and the other precious metals lower. Silver would continue setting the tone for the market in the near term.
"All of this has to do with silver, which took a bit of a bath and went down from $5.00 to $4.90," a dealer said.
"You have to see what silver does. If it decides to go down, gold will go with it."
Silver was indicated unchanged from Thursday's London close at $4.90/$4.92 an ounce.
But silver would find initial support at recent lows around $4.85 if Thursday's losses, attributed to a sell-off by investment funds, were compounded, analysts said.

"Gold's burst of strength is running out of steam, as is that of platinum. But they should hold on support for now," technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
"But silver could soon try new lows," she added.

Several dealers said gold was expected to remain within the $380-$385 price band until after the end-of-month expiry of options, which give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell gold at a given price.
Platinum, which had climbed and then eased with gold this week, slumped further overnight in Asia.
Prices were at $384.00/$385.00 an ounce, down $1.60 from Thursday's London close, after hitting a high of $388.50 an ounce earlier in the week.
Its sister metal palladium was also easier at $116.50/$117.50 an ounce, down $0.75 from Thursday's close. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
